title: Choose the visual world for Landing Page
question: The roll assigned 16-bit Genesis Tomb Journal. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: 16-bit Tomb Journal
options.thesis: The landing page as a dusty, chunky pixel-art explorer's manual.
options.viewport: Title chiseled in a pixel wall, illuminated by animated torchlight with a glowing Press Start button.
options.risk: Might feel too heavy if the pixel art isn't readable.

raised.raise: The UI folds out like a crammed paper manual rather than scrolling endlessly.

options.label: Ancient Lapis Stargate
options.thesis: A mechanical puzzle lock made of gold and lapis lazuli.
options.viewport: A massive circular stone dial that clicks into place to reveal the game entry.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on. Beautiful but less pure-retro.

options.label: Dungeon Tape J-Card
options.thesis: Cramped, hand-inked aesthetic of a folded cassette manual.
options.viewport: The screen divided into narrow folding panels of lore and instructions.
options.case: Fuses well with retro gaming, but clashes with the warm desert Egyptian mandate.
options.risk: Grayscale palette might feel too bleak.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Standard clean landing page with an Egyptian background.
canonCard.viewport: A standard centered card layout over a static desert background.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from a normal web app.
